title: Choosing a flat Artinian subalgebra and elements of Lambda landing in it (the choice in the proof of Stacks 07FH)
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\Lambda$ a Noetherian $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal, $n\ge1$, and $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a local ring with maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak q\bar\Lambda$ and residue field $K=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Call a $k$-subalgebra $A\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ *admissible* if $A$ is an Artinian local ring, essentially of finite type over $k$ (isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to a localization $S^{-1}B$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] of a finitely generated $k$-algebra $B$ at a multiplicative subset $S\subseteq B$), the inclusion $A\to\bar\Lambda$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $\mathfrak m_A\bar\Lambda=\bar{\mathfrak m}$; then $\mathfrak m_A=A\cap\bar{\mathfrak m}$ and the residue field $F=A/\mathfrak m_A$ is a subfield of $K$ containing $k$. Let $A_0\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ be admissible. Then there are an admissible $A\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ with $A_0\subseteq A$, with residue field $F$, and elements $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_t\in\Lambda$ and $\lambda'_1,\dots,\lambda'_r\in\mathfrak q$ ($t,r\ge0$) such that: (a) the images of all $\lambda_j$ and $\lambda'_i$ in $\bar\Lambda$ lie in $A$ (so the residues $\bar\lambda_j\in K$ lie in $F$); (b) $\mathrm d\bar\lambda_1,\dots,\mathrm d\bar\lambda_t$ form a basis of the $F$-vector space $\Omega_{F/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; (c) the images of $\lambda'_1,\dots,\lambda'_r$ in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ generate the ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo), lines 2580-2603: 'Pick A ... see Lemma 07FG. ... Pick lambda_1,...,lambda_t in Lambda which map to elements of A in Lambda-bar such that moreover the images of d lambda_1,...,d lambda_t form a basis of Omega_{F/k}' and 'choose further elements lambda_{t+1},...,lambda_m in Lambda which map into A'. Stacks asserts these choices without argument, and for an arbitrary A they are impossible: Lambda=k[x,y], q=0, n=1, A=k(x/y) is admissible, but k[x,y] meets k(x/y) only in k, while Omega_{A/k} is nonzero; so A must be enlarged. Suggested proof (agent): take a_j in A_0 with d of their residues a basis of Omega_{F_0/k}, and generators b_i of m_{A_0} (n>=2; for n=1 take generators of q), write them as mu/s with a common s in Lambda minus q, and enlarge A_0 according to the residue alpha of s exactly as in the three cases of the proof of Lemma 07FI (alpha transcendental over F_0: A=A_0[s-bar] localized, add s to the lambda's; alpha algebraic: Q=p^e >= n with alpha^Q separable over F_0, a finite etale A over A_0 with residue field F_0(alpha^Q) containing s-bar^N, N a power of p, and use mu s^(N-1), whose differentials are alpha^N d(residue))

proof.text: Apply the quotient-basis enlargement theorem. It provides an admissible local subalgebra A containing A₀, finite families with specified images in A, a basis of residue differentials, and generation of the ambient maximal ideal in the quotient.

Put L = Λ_q, m = qL and π : L → L/m^n. Since n ≥ 1, m^n ≤ m. Lift the residue map L → κ(q) through π to a k-algebra homomorphism f, whose kernel is m.map π. Admissibility gives m_A.map A.val = m.map π. Thus m_A ≤ comap A.val (ker f); the latter ideal is proper because the composite map to κ(q) is unital. Maximality of m_A gives equality. Descend f restricted to A through m_A; the resulting field homomorphism is injective, and evaluating its lift on a residue gives the required compatibility for every x ∈ L.

If n = 1, choose a finite generating family zs of q by Noetherianity. Its images vanish in L/m, hence lie in A with lifts zero. Mapping the equality span(zs)=q into L proves the localized generator conclusion. This replaces the quotient-level generator family, whose empty choice would supply no information in this case.

If n ≥ 2 let J be the span in L of the generator images supplied by the enlargement. Membership in q gives J ≤ m. Equality after applying π and the quotient ideal correspondence give m ≤ J + m^n. Since m^n ≤ m², m ≤ J + m • m. The ideal m is finitely generated by Noetherianity and lies in the Jacobson radical of L since L is local. Apply Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot to obtain m ≤ J, hence J=m. Keep the differential-basis family and all its specified lifts unchanged.

split_report.summary: Proved (statement kept unchanged). Route of the lead_note: choose a_j in A_0 with dc_j a basis of Omega_{F_0/k} (finite by 07E1), generators b_i of m_{A_0} (n>=2) or of q (n=1), a common denominator s in Lambda minus q; enlarge A_0 by the residue alpha of s as in the proof of 07FI, case T (alpha transcendental: A=A_0[t] localized, s-bar in A, Omega basis dc_j, d alpha via 00RS-type polynomial extension and localization of differentials) or case S (alpha algebraic: finite etale extension with residue F_0(alpha^Q) separable, embedded by the henselian retraction, s-bar^N in A for a p-power N>=p, Omega basis dc_j by Jacobi-Zariski with H_1 = Omega = 0 for F/F_0 etale); the case alpha in F_0 is included in S (Q=1). Flatness of the enlarged ring into Lambda-bar by 00MP and injectivity by faithful flatness, as in 07FI. lambda_j = mu_j s^(N-1) (residue c_j alpha^N, differential alpha^N dc_j as p | N) plus s in case T; lambda'_i = mu'_i s^(N-1) generating q Lambda_q by Nakayama (n>=2). The statement is true; no new node: every step cites existing nodes (those of the 07FI split for the enlargement). Note: lem-weil-pbc-popescu-enlarge-solution-modulo (07FI) is stated for the D of 07FH's conclusion although its proof uses only that D -> Lambda-bar is a flat local map of Artinian local rings; it could not be cited for an admissible A_0, so its case argument is repeated here (steps 7, 8, 10-12).

reviewed.note: 15 steps (agent proof; the node was created today to close the gap in Stacks 07FH): setup and the parenthetical claims; a basis dc_j of Omega_{F_0/k} (finite by 07E1) with lifts a_j in A_0; generators of m_{A_0} (n >= 2) or of q (n = 1); a common denominator s with residue alpha; the claim that an element with nonzero residue in the residue field of a local subring has its q-th power in it for q = p^e >= n (L checked: (1+eps)^q = 1 + eps^q = 1); case T (alpha transcendental): A = the image of A_0[t]_n, flat by the local criterion, faithfully flat hence injective, essentially of finite type via 07DT (3), residue field F_0(alpha) with basis dc_j, d alpha (polynomial extension and localization of differentials); case S (alpha algebraic): beta = alpha^Q separable, F_1 = F_0(beta) lifted to a finite etale A_0-algebra by the henselian equivalence (04GK node), embedded into Lambda-bar by the henselian retraction (04GG (8) node) since Lambda-bar is Artinian hence henselian, flat as before, s-bar^N in A by the claim, basis dc_j of Omega_{F/k} by Jacobi-Zariski with F/F_0 etale; lambda_j = mu_j s^{N-1} (and s in case T), residues c_j alpha^N with d(alpha^N) = 0 as p | N, giving (a), (b); lambda'_i = mu'_i s^{N-1} generating q Lambda_q by Nakayama (n >= 2), giving (c). L checked every hypothesis of the flatness criterion, of the henselian nodes and of the p-th power claim.
